basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 1.' and it opens '| Vers. 1. Abraham vero duxit aliam uxorem Ceturam. Quae interpretatur copulata vel'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: | Vers. 1. Abraham vero duxit aliam uxorem Ceturam. Quae interpretatur copulata vel conjuncta. Unde tradunt Hebraei hanc esse Agar matrem Ismaelis quae prius concubina fuerat, sed post mortem Sarae Abrahae legitime copulabatur: quod ideo fingunt, ut excusent Abraham ne jam senex et depositus novis nuptiis videatur lascivisse.
